narration.full_text: Hello students! In this section, we'll dive into the fascinating world of control and coordination in living organisms. We'll explore how different activities are regulated and integrated to ensure survival and proper responses to the environment. Control and coordination is the process by which different activities of an organism are regulated and integrated so that it can respond properly to internal and external stimuli. Living organisms perform many activities at the same time. These activities must be controlled and coordinated to maintain balance and survival. All living organisms respond and react to changes in the environment around them. These changes are called stimuli. Stimuli can be anything from light, heat, cold, smell, or touch. Both plants and animals respond to stimuli, but they do so in different ways. In animals, control and coordination are primarily managed by two main systems: the Nervous system and the Endocrine system. Today, we will focus on the Nervous System.

Definition of Control and Coordination: The process by which different activities of an organism are regulated and integrated so that it can respond properly to internal and external stimuli. Importance: Maintain balance and survival.
Definition of Stimuli: Changes in the environment to which organisms respond and react (e.g., light, heat, cold, smell, touch). Note: Both plants and animals respond to stimuli differently.
